new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Network Convenings
new_jobs.description:
About the Organization - Beyond100K

To solve the world's most pressing problems, we need tomorrow's problem-solvers equipped with Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) knowledge, skills, and inspiration. And tomorrow's problem-solvers need excellent STEM teachers today to guide them. In 2021, Beyond100K (formerly 100Kin10) successfully met its first 10-year goal by preparing more than 108,000 excellent STEM teachers for America's classrooms, surpassing the audacious goal set by President Obama a decade prior. To do this, we built a new type of networked-impact effort that rethinks how organizations collaborate, learn from one another, and together identify and tackle challenges that none could successfully address on its own. We achieved this goal in the midst of a growing national teacher shortage and a global pandemic, uniting over 300 leading agencies and organizations and 3,000 individuals across the country to tackle something seemingly intractable — ending the STEM teacher shortage, so that all kids could have access to a great STEM education and contribute their spark to a brighter future.

Beyond100K
- To decide our next goal, we undertook a national, participatory listening process asking young people, primarily Black, Latinx, and Native American young people, to share their experience in PK-12 STEM education. More than 600 young people responded to our call . Their stories and the resulting goal position us to decrease the STEM teacher shortage and center belonging, while focusing on the students, teachers, and schools that have been least well-served in STEM education. By 2032, our goal is to increase student and teacher belonging and to reduce the shortage by one-third, mobilizing a growing network to prepare 150,000 STEM teachers and retain 150,000 STEM teachers beginning with schools in Black, Latinx, and Native American communities — where the shortage has been the hardest to solve.

How we work now
- We pursue that goal through our whole network programming as well as our CoLabs: bounded communities of partners who go deep on one high-leverage challenge. Four CoLabs are underway: Classrooms of Belonging / AI, Foundational Math, Dream to Teach, and Teacher Work Environment, surrounded by whole-network programming that helps partners find one another, share what works, and carry it into the field while anchoring in our moonshot goal.

About the Role

The Network Community Team is focused on how partners find their way into Beyond100k, how they meet each other and connect in the network, and design community building experiences that strengthen connections and relationships between partners so that good work travels without us in the middle. We are seeking a Program Manager to lead the experience design of our whole-network convening spaces: the gatherings, spaces of learning, inspiration, and connection that turn more than 250 partner organizations into an actual network rather than a list.
The core of the role is designing how we bring people together both in person and virtually. You will design and manage our network gatherings including our flagship annual summit, regional meet-ups, virtual learning sessions, and strategize with the network community team to develop pathways for partners to deepen their engagement through 1:1 connection, our virtual community platform, and through deeper engagement into our micro-communities.

Expected travel is 10-15%
and includes bi-annual team retreats, our annual Summit and partner convening, regional meet-ups, and select in-person partner engagements. The Program Manager sits within the Network Community Team, and reports to the Associate Director, Network Development & Impact.

Your Responsibilities will Include

Network Gatherings and Events

Lead the user-experience design, strategy, budgeting, and delivery of whole-network gatherings including virtual convenings such as our annual network launch and new partner onboarding, and our annual in-person Summit, from concept to implementation to follow-up.
Design the participant experience, session architecture, and the partner journey through all whole network Beyond100K events, grounding in equitable and human-centered design.
Lead event execution: produce smaller and virtual gatherings and manage our event vendors to deliver the Summit and other large events on time and on budget.
Own the convening calendar: what we gather people for, how often, in what format, ensuring that we have a consistent cadence of events throughout the year in support of our goals.
Manage internal stakeholders, event vendors, venues, and consultants as needed across the gathering portfolio.
Evaluate gathering and program outcomes and partner engagement, and use what you find to change what we do next.

Community Design and Activation

Support the development of engagement pathways that move partners into deeper contributions and peer connection over time along with members of the network community team.
Design recruitment and mobilization strategies for whole-network programs and events, against defined participation targets, work collaboratively with the Network Coordinator to execute on the plan.
Set the strategy and design for Circle, our network community platform, what the space is for, how it is structured, and what strong engagement looks like.

Contribute to the Strategy and Design for Other Partner Touchpoints

Act as a thought partner and expert on other key partner experiences checking for alignment with the CoLab calendar.
Support whole-network program outcomes and opportunities through progress monitoring, evaluation, and coordination with internal teammates, external vendors, consultants, and network partners.

Your Experience

The ideal candidate will have a minimum of four years of related professional experience, including experience in the following areas:
Equitable and human centered design practitioner
Designing and delivering convenings and events, virtual and in person, at a range of sizes, including at least one flagship-scale event you were responsible for.
Program design and management in one of the following areas: adult learning, leadership development, network or community management, and/or community organizing along with group facilitation experience (in-person and virtual).
Managing virtual communities or networks, including responsibility for engagement and participation outcomes.
Managing vendors, consultants, and event budgets.
Nice to have: Experience in STEM education, K-12 or teacher-focused organizations, or a membership or network organization.

Skills

Project & Program Manager:
You have demonstrated program and project management skills. You are highly organized with strong follow-through, and you nail the details, so nothing falls through the cracks on a complex, high-visibility event.
Experience Designer:
You design experiences that build community. You craft, produce, and facilitate inclusive, engaging and memorable gatherings that bring diverse groups of organizations and individuals together, and that inspire, delight, and catalyze action.
Analytical Problem-Solver:
You use data and partner feedback to understand what is working, diagnose what is not, and make sound decisions. When plans change or problems come up, you find practical solutions quickly.
Strategic Communicator & Facilitator:
You are an excellent communicator. You excel at facilitating rich conversations on complex issues and synthesizing insights from gatherings.
Impact Player & Team Member:
You are able to work independently and as part of a remote team. You are self-directed and proactive in an environment with dynamic priorities. You are team-oriented, open-minded, creative and flexible.

Mindsets

Solution-Oriented:
You focus on what will work. You ask good questions, test ideas, gather data, and adjust course, and you are never afraid to rethink an approach.
Continuous Improvement:
You are someone who is continually striving to improve and regularly create and take advantage of learning opportunities. You collect data and determine opportunities to better meet the needs of partners and the Network.
People First:
You lead with a human-centered approach, with colleagues and network partners alike .
You prioritize relationships with individuals and organizations and believe in the power of bringing groups together around a common charge.
Self-motivation:
The drive to proactively take the initiative, identifying problems and opportunities across your portfolio, developing recommendations, and taking action on those recommendations.
Adaptability:
The ability to thrive in an ambiguous environment where you have autonomy to drive your work.
Passion for Social Change:
The drive to contribute to change in education and beyond, and the ability to lead and design in a way that is centered on racial justice and diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Working at Beyond100K

People who thrive at Beyond100K are team-oriented, open-minded, creative, and flexible and possess a strong desire to learn and grow in a feedback-rich remote work environment. Our culture embraces colleagues with genuine warmth, a curiosity to learn, a drive toward excellence, the ability to laugh at themselves, an eagerness for feedback to spur growth and impact, and an interest in co-workers as colleagues and as human beings.

We believe in community. We believe that diverse perspectives and backgrounds create a rich work environment that is essential to our work. We are committed to building an organization with raised consciousness in order to impact how we collaborate with our partners, support our network, and work together as a team. We aim to build each other up, empower each other, and give each other what we need to grow and thrive. We hope you will join us as we continue to build a diverse organization that fosters a work environment where people from all backgrounds are welcomed, valued, and supported.

The salary band for this role is $ 75,500-$85,500
. This role will pay in that band, commensurate to the experience of the individual who is hired. Beyond100K offers a comprehensive benefits program that includes medical, dental, vision, life, short-term & long-term disability, and a 403(b) retirement plan with up to 5% employer match. We also offer 15 paid vacation days in the first year and 20 vacation days in year 2, plus 12 observed holidays. Additionally, our offices are closed between December 25th and January 1st.

new_jobs.title: Oracle Technical Project Manager — E-Business Suite and Fusion
new_jobs.description:
Center of Excellence | Working alongside Tessera AI Agents

Remote, USA

Location:
Near-shore (Latin America) or offshore (e.g., India). Both are open, and we will evaluate strong candidates from either.

Remote:
Yes, with a daily overlap of US business hours (full overlap for near-shore, at least 3–4 hours for offshore) and occasional travel to customer sites for kick-offs and go-lives as needed.

Experience:
12+ years

Employment type:
Long-term contract, engaged directly or through a staffing partner.

Positions:
1

Start date:
Immediate.

Engagement model:
Multi-engagement delivery management role. Approximately 80% running several concurrent Oracle engagements — proofs of value, discovery and implementation work across E-Business Suite and Fusion — and 20% delivery standards, platform input and pre-sales support. Works with a daily overlap of US business hours alongside customers, Oracle architects and SMEs, Forward Deployed Engineers and the Principal Architects.

About Tessera Labs

Tessera is an AI-native platform for enterprise transformation. The multi-agent platform delivers governed execution across ERP, CRM, HCM, and finance systems, cutting timelines from years to weeks and costs by more than half. Built on deep expertise across Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, Workday, and other systems of record, Tessera address the scope a system integrator would have traditionally taken up with the speed of execution and efficiency of an AI-native platform.

For decades, enterprises have struggled with fragmented business systems, where migrations have consumed hundreds of millions of dollars, data stayed inconsistent and unreliable, and business processes slowed under manual review. Tessera was founded to change that, for Oracle and every other system enterprises depend on. The name itself — a tessera, a single tile in a mosaic — reflects our mission: unifying the disparate pieces of the enterprise into a coherent whole. Tessera is an AI-powered, multi-agent platform that harmonizes systems and lets teams work in plain English.

Role Summary

We are looking for an Oracle Technical Project Manager to run Oracle E-Business Suite and Oracle Fusion Cloud engagements — several at the same time — from kick-off to go-live. Our architects decide what the solution should be; you make sure it gets built, tested, converted and cut over on the date we committed to, and that the customer can see exactly where it stands at every point in between.

This is a technical project management role, and that is deliberate. You need to know Oracle delivery well enough to manage the deliverables themselves, not just the dates: the RICEFW inventory, functional and technical specifications, configuration moving between environments, data conversion mock cycles, integration builds, test cycles and the cutover runbook. A project manager who cannot tell whether a mock conversion actually reconciled, or why a Fusion quarterly update threatens the test plan, will report green until the week it turns red.

Most of our customers are not simply upgrading Oracle. They come from SAP ECC, JD Edwards, PeopleSoft, Infor or home-grown systems, and many run EBS and Fusion side by side. Our engagements are also shorter and sharper than a traditional system integrator’s: proofs of value measured in weeks, with success criteria agreed up front and evidence of value expected at the end.

You will run these engagements with Tessera’s AI agents as part of the team, and you need to be genuinely fluent in using AI. The platform produces a large share of the analysis, specifications, configuration, code and test material. Your job is to plan around that: build review and approval gates into the plan, know where AI output needs a domain expert’s eye, track the value it delivers against the manual baseline, and use AI tools yourself to plan, report and spot risk faster. What the platform cannot do is hold a steering committee to a decision or tell a customer that the date is at risk. That is the role.

Two outcomes define the job. The first is engagements that land: on the date, inside the scope, with the customer’s sign-off and a reference we can use. The second is that each one makes the next easier to run, because what you learn goes into our delivery standards and the platform rather than staying in your head.

Key Responsibilities

Engagement Planning and Governance (25%)
Own the plan on several concurrent Oracle engagements: scope, phases, milestones, dependencies, resourcing and the critical path — from discovery and fit-gap through build, testing, data conversion, cutover and hypercare.
Set up and run governance: weekly checkpoints, daily syncs during execution, steering committees, RAID logs and clear escalation paths — and report status the customer’s executives can trust.
Manage scope, budget and commercial terms: burn and forecast against fixed-fee and time-and-materials engagements, change requests and change orders, with no surprises for the client partner or the customer.
Agree success criteria for proofs of value up front and track them through to an evidence-based close-out.
Management of Technical Deliverables (35%)
Own the RICEFW inventory (reports, interfaces, conversions, extensions, forms and workflows) and drive each item through specification, build, review, test and sign-off.
Manage functional and technical specifications, code and configuration as deliverables — with review gates, quality criteria and traceability from requirement to test.
Plan and control environments and configuration movement: EBS instance strategy, cloning and patch windows (including R12.2 online patching); Fusion environment refreshes, Functional Setup Manager migrations and the quarterly update cycle.
Run data conversion as a managed workstream: mock conversion cycles, reconciliation sign-off, defect tracking and readiness criteria for each load.
Coordinate integration builds and third-party dependencies — banks, tax engines, payroll, EDI and legacy systems — and the testing between them.
Lead test management (CRPs, SIT, UAT, regression for Fusion quarterly updates) with entry and exit criteria, defect triage cadence and go/no-go evidence.
Plan and run cutover: an hour-by-hour runbook, rehearsals, go/no-go criteria, rollback and contingency plans, and hypercare.
AI-Enabled Delivery (20%)
Plan engagements around AI-generated work: where the Tessera platform produces analysis, specifications, configuration, code and test scripts, and where human review and approval gates sit in the schedule.
Work with Tessera’s Forward Deployed Engineers and domain SMEs to keep AI output grounded and validated, and escalate early when a deliverable needs expert attention.
Measure and report the value AI delivers — time and effort saved against the manual baseline, quality of output, and adoption by the customer’s team.
Use AI tools in your own work every day: drafting plans, status reports and meeting summaries, analysing risks and dependencies, and preparing steering committee material.
Apply sound judgment on data privacy and security when AI is used on customer data, in line with the customer’s policies and our agreements.
Client Leadership, Standards and Pre-Sales (20%)
Be the primary delivery counterpart for the customer’s program office and IT leadership, and build the trust that turns a proof of value into a follow-on engagement.
Manage organisational change and readiness with the customer: training, communication and business sign-offs, so go-live is adopted, not just executed.
Contribute to Tessera’s Oracle delivery standards — plan templates, RACI, governance packs, cutover runbooks and lessons learned — and feed field input to the platform team.
Support pre-sales with delivery plans, staffing models, timelines and risk assessments for proposals and statements of work.

Required Qualifications

12+ years in project or program management, including at least three full-lifecycle Oracle ERP implementations as project manager — covering both Oracle E-Business Suite (R12.x) and Oracle Fusion Cloud, at least one of each.
At least one engagement where the customer moved to Oracle from a different ERP, such as SAP ECC, JD Edwards, PeopleSoft or Infor.
Hands-on experience managing technical deliverables on Oracle implementations: RICEFW inventories, functional and technical specifications, configuration migration, data conversion mock cycles, integrations, test cycles and cutover runbooks.
Working knowledge of Oracle delivery methods — Oracle Unified Method (OUM) for EBS and Oracle’s cloud implementation approach for Fusion — and of the Fusion quarterly update cycle and Oracle Support service request management.
Practical, everyday fluency with AI: using generative AI and agentic tools in your own work, and experience — or a clear point of view — on planning and governing delivery where AI produces part of the work.
Strong commercial and governance discipline: budgets, burn and forecast, change control, RAID management and steering committees.
Senior client-facing presence: able to hold a steering committee, deliver bad news early and keep the relationship.
Proven ability to run several engagements at once without losing control of any of them.
Proven ability to learn a new AI platform quickly and become the person others ask. You will be expected to reach real fluency in the Tessera platform within your first months.
Excellent verbal and written business English, with strong presentation ability to both business and technical audiences.
Experience leading distributed (onshore, nearshore and offshore) delivery teams, with strong asynchronous communication discipline.
Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Who This Role Is Not For

If your project management stops at the plan and the status report, this is not the role — you will be expected to understand and manage the technical deliverables themselves. If you have run ERP programs but never an Oracle implementation through cutover, you will find the learning curve steep on our timelines. If you are sceptical of AI or prefer to keep it at arm’s length, you will struggle in a delivery model where AI agents produce a large share of the work. And if you want one long program with a scope someone else agreed, you will find several short, high-pressure engagements uncomfortable.

Preferred Qualifications

A technical or functional background in Oracle before moving into project management — for example as a developer, DBA, data conversion lead or module consultant.
Experience running proofs of value or pilot engagements with defined success criteria and measured outcomes.
Experience with AI or automation tooling in ERP delivery — code generation, test automation, data quality or documentation tools — and with measuring its impact.
Agile or hybrid delivery experience, and tooling such as Jira, Smartsheet, MS Project or Confluence.
PMP, PRINCE2, PgMP or SAFe certification.
Oracle Fusion Cloud implementation certification or Oracle Cloud Success Navigator experience.
Experience with large multi-country or multi-entity Oracle rollouts, and with system integrator and staffing partner management.
Experience running engagements for US or European customers from a near-shore or offshore location, with strong ownership despite the time-zone gap.
Spanish, Portuguese or German is a plus but not a must-have.

First-Year Measures of Success

Month 1: Fluent in the Tessera platform. Running at least one Oracle engagement with plan, governance, RAID log and success criteria agreed with the customer.
Month 3: Running at least two engagements on plan, with technical deliverables, AI review gates and value metrics tracked and reported, and a first set of Tessera Oracle delivery templates in use across the team.

Certification & Licensure Support

Provide support for assessment-related resources, systems, and activities designed to promote successful completion of required assessments.

new_jobs.title: Business Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Description

Are you an organized and analytical professional who enjoys improving business processes, coordinating across teams, and helping others make effective use of business applications and data? Do you thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where accuracy, follow-through, and continuous improvement matter? If so, we’re looking for someone like you to join APL’s Finance Strategy & Operations team as a Business Operations Analyst in our Data Analytics Section.

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL.

In this role, you will support business operations across the Business, Construction, and Facilities Department by helping coordinate the department’s use of Oracle E-Business Suite and related business applications. You will work with stakeholders to understand issues, document business needs, support system and process changes, coordinate testing and communications, and maintain clear procedures and reference materials. You will also develop expertise in Procurement and Accounting processes and data, perform analysis and reconciliation, and contribute to cross-functional initiatives that improve service, efficiency, data quality, and decision-making.

This position is well suited for a professional who enjoys learning complex business processes, organizing work across multiple stakeholders, and using data and business applications to solve operational problems. Over time, you will have opportunities to develop deeper expertise in enterprise applications, Procurement and Accounting data, business analysis, and process improvement.

As a Business Operations Analyst, You Will

Serve as the primary day-to-day business liaison for APL’s Oracle E-Business Suite enterprise resource planning application, assessing and triaging reported issues, directing them to the appropriate business or technical teams, and coordinating follow-up through resolution.
Gather, clarify, analyze, and document business, system, data, and reporting requirements for application enhancements, analytics efforts, and process-improvement initiatives.
Develop working expertise in Procurement and Accounting processes, data, business definitions, and relevant ERP data structures, helping stakeholders improve the consistency, traceability, and effective use of their data.
Analyze, validate, and reconcile ERP and operational data to identify discrepancies, investigate root causes, and support accurate reporting, reliable business processes, and informed decision-making.
Partner with Procurement, Contracts, Accounting, Finance, and IT to connect business processes, systems, and data and support cohesive solutions across the organization.
Develop and maintain process documentation, data definitions, user communications, and training resources to promote consistent system use and maintain effective operational coverage.
Identify opportunities to streamline, standardize, automate, or redesign recurring business and system processes, while also contributing to data requests, ad hoc analysis, special projects, and cross-functional initiatives

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you:

Possess a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Systems Engineering, or a related field, and have at least two years of relevant professional experience in business systems, business analysis, data analysis, finance, accounting, procurement, operations, or a related area.
Have experience supporting a complex business application or data-dependent business process, including assessing issues, coordinating resolution, documenting processes, or supporting system and process changes.
Demonstrate strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to investigate discrepancies, evaluate information from multiple sources, and identify potential root causes.
Have experience gathering, clarifying, and documenting business, system, data, or reporting requirements and supporting related testing, implementation, or process-change activities.
Show proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, especially Excel, and have experience analyzing, validating, and reconciling data with a strong emphasis on accuracy and consistency.
Communicate clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing, and are comfortable working with business users, technical teams, analysts, and organizational leadership.
Are detail oriented, well organized, and able to manage multiple priorities, maintain effective documentation, and follow issues and assignments through resolution.
Hold US Citizenship or permanent resident status, as required to access APL’s facilities and networks, subject to applicable laws

You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you:

Experience supporting Oracle E-Business Suite or another enterprise resource planning system from the business or functional side, particularly within Procurement, Accounting, Projects, Contracts, or related financial modules.
Experience performing business systems analysis activities such as triaging application issues, gathering requirements, coordinating enhancements, developing test scenarios, supporting user acceptance testing, or preparing user documentation and training.
Knowledge of Procurement, Accounting, financial management, or related business processes, including how business rules and transactions affect downstream data, reporting, and decision-making.
Experience using SQL and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau to analyze, reconcile, validate, or present data.
Experience with data definitions, data lineage, data quality, data governance, process mapping, process improvement, or workflow automation.
Familiarity with internal controls, audit requirements, government contracting, or another regulated financial or operational environment.

The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. Description

Amazon Global Corporate Communications (GCC) is looking for a Senior Program Manager to lead the data and AI systems that GCC's teams rely on. You'll build the shared foundation beneath GCC's work: making its data usable by AI, delivering the AI systems on top of it, and connecting the work across GCC and its partners.

Today, a lot of GCC's most valuable data is scattered. Research, media coverage, agency reporting, processes, and planning documents live in different places and formats, with different access. That makes it hard for teams to bring it together, and hard for AI to do anything with it. You'll connect those sources, structure them so AI can actually retrieve and reason over the content, and design tools on top of them. The teams who produce the data still own it. You make sure it's structured, accessible, and fits together, so everyone gets more out of it.

A lot of this job comes down to giving people across the team more ownership of their work. That happens two ways. First, by reducing dependencies, the places where people are stuck waiting on a manual step, a handoff, or the one person who knows how something works. Second, by clearing away the rote, repetitive work that fills their days. You'll get to know how GCC operates, find where both of these slow people down, and build what it takes to help. Everyone here is a builder, and your job is to support that.

No two months in this role look the same. The data keeps growing, the tools keep changing, and there's always a new challenge worth taking on. It's a great fit for someone who likes to work independently, dig into complex problems, and see their work make a difference across a team.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience in complex problem solving, and working in a tight schedule environment

Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

Your work will directly improve the quality, velocity, reliability, and cost efficiency of the data used to train and validate mass-market autonomous-driving systems.

Define and manage the roadmap for the autonomous-driving training data lake, covering data collection, ingestion, processing, storage, curation, and delivery.
Coordinate execution across data infrastructure, machine learning, annotation, simulation, and autonomous-driving algorithm teams.
Establish and track KPIs for data quality, pipeline reliability, processing latency, dataset readiness, storage efficiency, and infrastructure cost.
Drive programs for dataset generation, versioning, metadata management, lineage, and reproducibility.
Identify technical risks and bottlenecks in data pipelines, infrastructure capacity, and training-data delivery, and lead cross-functional resolution.
Improve engineering planning, agile development practices, dependency management, and operational processes across data platform teams.

Bachelors or Masters in computer science or other related engineering field.
5 years + of technical program management experience in engineering or related fields.
Experience leading complex cross-functional data, infrastructure, software, or machine learning programs.
Strong understanding of large-scale data systems, cloud infrastructure, and data pipelines.
Mandarin speaking is required.

Excellent problem-solving skills.
Strong understanding of large-scale data systems, cloud infrastructure, and data pipelines.
Experience in establishing strong software development processes.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with autonomous-driving data platforms, machine learning infrastructure, or large-scale training-data systems.
Experience managing large-scale data lakes, distributed data pipelines, or cloud infrastructure programs.
Familiarity with data technologies such as object storage, Spark, Ray, Kafka, Iceberg, Parquet, Kubernetes, or similar systems.
Understanding of machine learning data workflows, including data curation, annotation, training, evaluation, and closed-loop improvement.
Experience managing complex cross-functional programs across multiple teams, locations, or time zones.

What do we provide:

A fun, supportive and engaging environment.
Opportunity to make a significant impact on the transportation revolution by the means of advancing autonomous driving.
Opportunity to work on cutting edge technologies with the top talent in the field.
Competitive compensation package.
Snacks, lunches, dinners and fun activities.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager (Data Centers)
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Project Manager (Data Centers)
to join us in Houston, TX.
The following locations will also be considered: San Diego, CA, Herndon, VA, New York, NY, Houston, TX, Portland, OR and Seattle, WA
. This position can be offered remotely.

As demand for AI, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure accelerates, our clients are developing some of the world's largest, most complex, and most power-intensive facilities. In this role, you will help deliver the electrical infrastructure that enables next-generation data center campuses—projects requiring hundreds of megawatts of power and unprecedented levels of planning, engineering, and coordination. You will work across the full project lifecycle, playing a key role in delivering critical infrastructure for some of the industry's most prominent clients.

What makes this opportunity unique is the breadth of collaboration across WSP's global organization. You will work alongside top experts in their field to solve highly complex infrastructure challenges. This multidisciplinary environment provides exposure to the full range of technical and strategic considerations required to successfully develop large-scale data center campuses. You will contribute to the planning and design of substations, transmission interconnections, and site electrical infrastructure while supporting fast-paced projects that demand innovation, technical excellence, and strong collaboration.

If you're energized by large-scale infrastructure projects, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and want to help shape the future of digital infrastructure, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact while accelerating your career on some of the most significant power delivery projects being developed today.

Provides technical project supervision and guidance in managing the administrative, commercial, and technical components of critical high-voltage infrastructure for data center projects in alignment with WSP’s core values and contractual commitments. Tasks include responsibility for overall performance of distribution system and grid modernization projects of moderate size/complexity and/or local/regional scope. Oversight includes financial performance, technical execution, client satisfaction, quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC), safety, and schedule adherence.

Ensures that responsibilities throughout the full project lifecycle (feasibility, engineering design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout) are executed in compliance with corporate standards, regulatory requirements (e.g., NERC, IEEE, NEC), and utility industry best practices.

Your Impact

Lead and oversee cross-functional teams delivering power distribution and utility engineering projects, ensuring execution of design and construction deliverables.
Manage multiple concurrent projects involving distribution lines, feeders, and grid infrastructure upgrades, including budgets, schedule, cost control, and resource allocation.
Develop and manage project scopes, cost estimates, schedules, and resource plans for utility capital improvement programs and distribution projects.
Build and maintain Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) aligned with engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) project delivery models.
Ensure compliance with utility standards, environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and safety protocols (OSHA, utility HSE standards).
Participate in proposal development, RFP responses, and business development efforts within the power & energy market.
Perform margin analysis, risk assessments, and contingency planning for power delivery projects.
Coordinate contract negotiations, client presentations, and stakeholder meetings with utilities, municipalities, and regulatory agencies.
Develop and maintain project plans including PMP, Safety Plans, Risk Management Plans, and QA/QC procedures.
Collaborate with engineering teams specializing in all aspects of distribution design.
Partner with Project Accounting to manage financials including forecasting, earned value management (EVM), and profitability tracking.
Lead efforts in change management, scope control, and claims mitigation.
Coordinate with technical managers on staffing for overhead and underground distribution projects.
Ensure adherence to health, safety, and environmental (HSE) standards, escalating issues when necessary.
Provide reporting to clients and leadership on project performance, risks, schedule, and budget status.
Manage project closeout activities, including lessons learned and continuous improvement for future projects.
Stay current on power industry trends, grid resilience, distributed energy resources (DER), and electrification initiatives.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or related field or 7+ years of relevant experience in lieu of degree.
7+ years of experience managing projects in power distribution, transmission & distribution (T&D), or utility engineering environments.
Proven experience delivering feeder, distribution line, or grid modernization projects.
Strong understanding of utility operations, power systems engineering, and electrical distribution design.
Familiarity with NERC, IEEE standards, NEC codes, and utility regulatory requirements.
Experience with EPC project delivery, capital programs, and infrastructure projects within the energy sector.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills in complex utility environments.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills working with utilities, clients, regulators, and internal engineering teams.
Experience with project management tools (MS Project, Primavera P6), financial tracking, and reporting systems.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams including engineering, design, procurement, and construction professionals.
Knowledge of QA/QC processes, risk management, and safety compliance in utility projects.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Professional Engineer (PE) license.
PMI Certification (PMP or CAPM).

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation

Expected Salary (all locations): $102,200 - $182,200

WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

new_jobs.description:
Description

Penn Medicine is dedicated to our tripartite mission of providing the highest level of care to patients, conducting innovative research, and educating future leaders in the field of medicine. Working for this leading academic medical center means collaboration with top clinical, technical and business professionals across all disciplines.

Today at Penn Medicine, someone will make a breakthrough. Someone will heal a heart, deliver hopeful news, and give comfort and reassurance. Our employees shape our future each day. Are you living your life's work?

Entity
: Corporate Services

Department
: Materials Management Administration

Location
: 3535 Market

Hours
: Remote, M-F, 8am-4:30pm ( may need to attend on site meetings in occasion)

Summary
:

The Supply Chain Project Manager reports to the Vice President of Supply Chain for UPHS. Their project focus is related to Supply Chain priority projects primarily revolving around standardization, consolidation, operational implementation of vendor or product changes, ERP functions, and performance improvement activities intended to improve financial sustainability. Their primary function is to Lead, guide and control the implementation of enterprise projects of medium risk, utilizing standard Project Management tools and methodologies. Manage project lifecycle for multiple enterprise projects and coordinate resources from corporate teams, physician teams, clinical teams, IT teams, operational areas, external consultants and vendors. Ongoing project responsibilities include overseeing the project budget, resource management, scope management, development and management of the project schedule, coordination with hospital departments and staff, training, change management, communication management, risk assessment and mitigation, and issue resolution. Advocate on behalf of the patient ensuring that requirements are met and services rendered by clinicians are not adversely impacted by new processes or systems. Ensure the delivery of projects on scope and on time. Provide project leadership and direction, give guidance to project teams on how to navigate barriers related to resources, timing, implementation and competing priorities and escalating issues to leadership when appropriate. Performs job functions with minimal oversight.

Accountabilities

Responsible for coordination of projects and request for projects with SC leadership team, performing an initial analysis for leadership discussion related to resource allocation and project scoping
Provide leadership/direction for projects that have been assigned to her/him from VP of Supply Chain. Work with SC
Leaders across the enterprise to develop Project Governance, as needed, for each project. Develop project team with input from leadership. Lead, guide, assist and coordinate project team, users, vendors and other internal or external resources.
Manage the project schedule and meetings. Develop project scope. Assist with the development of cost/benefit data.
Develop and assist project team with application requirements and implementation tasks. Create project timeline & assign resources to tasks. Carry out timely and appropriate communication of project information to project stakeholders, project team and end users. Assist the team members to stay on task and escalate barriers to leadership when appropriate. Perform project close-out tasks, which includes obtaining approval to close the project and transitioning to an operational support model.
Monitor and control project issues and risks. Engage appropriate resources to resolve application development or implementation related issues. Support users/team members with problem solving. In all cases where appropriate develop and implement monitoring and compliance processes to assure sustainability of results.
Provide management and team project status reporting. Conduct well-managed and efficient Project Team meetings. Collaborate with project leads and assure alignment.
Prepare documentation for each project, appropriate to the project scope and length.
Assist with annual Supply Chain assigned strategic project planning process
Assist leadership with management and implementation of department standards, goal setting and prioritization of work.
Interface Supply Chain Teams, other department managers and operational staff on existing or proposed systems always fostering positive working relations and keeping customer satisfaction as primary goal.
Maintain strong project management skills. Stay current on best technology, best practices, processes and implementation methods.
Provide performance data to teams
Assist with internal process improvements, ERP Module updates and associated education.
Performs duties in accordance with Penn Medicine and entity values, policies, and procedures
Other duties as assigned to support the unit, department, entity, and health system organization

Minimum Requirements

Required Education and Experience

Bachelor's Degree Business administration, Supply Chain Management, Clinical Healthcare Roles, related field or equivalent experience is required.
5+ years Experience in each of the following is required for the position: Systems problem solving and analysis, managing implementations and conversions, and leading project teams is required.
3+ years Experience managing multiple concurrent projects is required.
3+ years Experience in Supply Chain is preferred.
4+ years Experience conducting meetings, preparing status reports, and supporting user/team members with problem solving, developing and coordinating with vendors on RFP’s/RFI’s is preferred.

Licenses, Registrations, and Certifications

Project Management Professional Certification preferred.

We believe that the best care for our patients starts with the best care for our employees. Our employee benefits programs help our employees get healthy and stay healthy. new_jobs.description:
At Accenture Federal Services, nothing matters more than helping the US federal government make the nation stronger and safer and life better for people. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations.

Join Accenture Federal Services, a technology company within global Accenture. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more.

Join us to drive positive, lasting change that moves missions and the government forward!

The work

As a Project Manager within Baseline, Standards and Requirements, you will drive clarity, alignment, and execution across functional delivery and strategic initiatives. You will oversee the full project lifecycle—from request intake and prioritization through delivery of high‑visibility operational and strategic efforts. This hands‑on, execution‑focused role requires managing complex stakeholder relationships, facilitating governance, and ensuring work is supported by clear documentation, data, and analysis. You will bring structure to ambiguous environments, maintain a high‑quality backlog or project portfolio, and provide teams with the direction and alignment necessary for successful delivery. Working across operational stakeholders, clinicians, technical teams, and senior leaders, you will ensure transparency, accountability, and high‑quality execution.

Key responsibilities:

Lead and organize project activities across the full lifecycle, ensuring requirements, priorities, timelines, and deliverables are clearly defined
Facilitate workshops, stakeholder discussions, and requirements‑gathering sessions to translate business needs into actionable documentation
Coordinate with cross‑functional teams to manage dependencies, negotiate priorities, and resolve issues
Drive clarity and structure in ambiguous or rapidly changing environments, identifying risks, gaps, and decision needs
Develop polished, executive‑ready communications including briefings, dashboards, and recommendations
Monitor progress and team performance, ensuring all inputs, requirements, and alignments are in place for effective execution
Support process improvement by enhancing intake flows, documentation standards, governance routines, and operational processes
Demonstrate strong communication and stakeholder management skills across clinical, technical, and executive audiences
Apply critical thinking and problem‑solving skills while managing multiple initiatives with high attention to detail
Foster collaboration, transparency, and accountability across all project participants

Here’s what you need:

5–8 years of experience as a Project Manager or Senior Business Analyst
Advanced understanding of Oracle Health (Cerner) or experience supporting federal healthcare organizations
Mastery of requirements gathering and backlog management
Deep experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies
PMP or Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) certification
Superior communication and negotiation skills
Bachelor’s degree in a related field

Eligibility requirements:

Must be a US Citizen
Must be eligible to obtain a Public Trust clearance
Must work on site at the VA (811 Vermont Ave, Washington DC) four (4) days per week if staffed at Project Reverence

. The base pay range for this position in these locations is shown below. $101,700—$204,400 USD

We have an unwavering commitment to creating a culture in which all our people are respected, feel a sense of belonging, and have equal opportunity. What we do

At BC Children’s Hospital Foundation, we’re on a quest to ensure every kid in the province receives the best health care imaginable. As a fundraising organization, we inspire communities and people to support BC Children’s Hospital, along with its world-class research institute, mental health facility and rehabilitation center.

Our work makes a profound difference. From helping get the boldest research ideas off the ground to supporting the most advanced equipment, together we are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in children’s health care. This is no small task—which is why we’re looking for passionate people to join our team and help propel our work forward to power the possible
.

In this newly created Project Manager role, you will help strengthen our ability to successfully deliver important projects across the Foundation. Reporting to the Program Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape a growing project delivery practice while working on varied, organization-wide initiatives. You’ll partner with people across the Foundation, influence meaningful change and see how thoughtful project leadership helps our teams move our cause forward.

More specifically, you will:
Build clear project plans that define what needs to be achieved, who is involved and how the work will move forward.
Lead projects from start to finish, bringing together people from across the Foundation and keeping work moving toward agreed outcomes.
Keep people informed and aligned by facilitating conversations, supporting decisions and communicating progress throughout the project.
Navigate challenges as they arise, identifying risks and roadblocks early and working with the right people to resolve them.
Support successful implementation by tracking progress, helping teams adapt to change and capturing lessons that strengthen future projects.

What you’ll bring

We understand that no single candidate will perfectly meet all the qualifications outlined for this job posting. The following highlights the qualifications we consider important:

A bachelor’s degree in business administration, project management, information systems or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience, along with formal project management training; a PMP or CAPM designation is considered an asset.
At least five years of project management experience, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional projects from planning through implementation.
Strong project management knowledge and skills, with the ability to create clear plans, keep work moving and guide projects toward successful outcomes.
Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with an ability to build trust, bring different perspectives together and effectively guide teams without formal authority.
Sound judgement and problem-solving skills, including the ability to navigate ambiguity, competing priorities and complex challenges.
Experience with Asana is strongly preferred. Experience in a non-profit or complex stakeholder environment, and experience with technical, systems or process implementation projects are considered assets.

What you can expect

Ensuring that kids receive the best health care imaginable is no small task, therefore taking care of our team is a top priority. To help you power the possible and to support you in your health, well-being, and career growth, in additional to competitive compensation, we offer perks like a hybrid work environment (minimum of two days per week in office) and nine-day fortnight schedule, generous vacation, topnotch health and dental benefits, a health care spending account, a defined benefit pension plan, and a commitment to professional development.

The hiring range for this position is between $91,100 to $101,800.
At BCCHF, we are committed to ensuring that compensation is fair and equitable. Your placement in the salary range will be determined by your experience, relevant skills, and qualifications as they relate to this role.

Please note that all team members of BCCHF are required to complete vulnerable sector criminal record check as a condition of employment.

Join us

We exist to power the possible . And that permeates every action we take. As a team, we push ourselves to: think big in how we are boldly envisioning the future; step up in how we are accountable to ourselves, each other and our shared cause; and lead with heart in how we listen and engage with others.

BCCHF invites and encourages all qualified individuals to apply. As an organization committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and support. We welcome individuals whose lived experiences may further contribute to the rich diversification of skills, knowledge, and backgrounds at the Foundation.

If this feels like the right fit for you, we’d love to hear from you. Join us in helping make kids mighty.

Apply online at www.bcchf.ca/join-our-team/ by November 15, 2026.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. new_jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Connected Warfare (Active Clearance)
new_jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time sensitive, multi domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kills chains and enable mission autonomy.

About The Job

Own overall program execution - meeting cost, schedule, and performance targets and exceeding program and warfighter expectations.
Acquire an intimate understanding of program requirements and maintain open dialogue with the customer to ensure engineering efforts remain aligned to mission objectives.
Develop and implement effective processes, tools, and metrics for program planning, scope management, risk management, and overall program execution.
Foster a “Team of Teams” culture amongst Anduril, external customers, and industry partners to align objectives, optimize processes, gather insight, and drive on-time execution.
Build an outcome-oriented, high-performance culture within the program team that values development velocity, high-trust collaboration, rigorous execution, and continuous improvement.
Drive cross-functional alignment efforts to ensure seamless integration across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, test and evaluation, operations, business development, and other Anduril teams.
Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from stakeholders. Demonstrate high ownership on all pieces of work. Become a trusted partner to Anduril’s engineers.
Support the drafting of technical proposals, ensuring that potential projects and scaling opportunities with each account are accurately scoped, resourced, and aligned with the organization's capabilities and strategic goals.

Key Responsibilities

In partnership with the Chief Engineer, own overall program execution, meeting cost, schedule, and performance targets and exceeding program and warfighter expectations. Monitor and manage program resource allocation, making tradeoffs that enable us to deliver best-in-class solutions to our customers on-time and on-budget.
Acquire an intimate understanding of program requirements and maintain open dialogue with the customer to ensure engineering efforts remain aligned to mission objectives.
Develop and implement effective processes, tools, and metrics for program planning, scope management, risk management, and overall program execution.
Drive cross-functional alignment efforts to ensure seamless integration across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, test and evaluation, operations, business development, and other Anduril teams.
Develop strong, trusting relationships with Anduril’s DoD customers, ensuring we have tight feedback loops that enable us to shape solutions, rapidly iterate, and ultimately field solutions faster.
Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from internal engineering, customers, and third-party partners to own successful delivery of outcomes on multiple programs simultaneously.
Develop and implement lightweight processes, tools, and metrics for program planning, scope management, risk management, and customer communication to enable Anduril to move rapidly.
Be high ownership on all pieces of work and become a trusted partner and advisor to Anduril’s engineers.
Foster a creative, high-performance culture within the team, and proactively assess team skills versus needs, identifying personnel development or recruitment opportunities to strengthen the team’s capabilities.

Qualifications And Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field (technical background preferred)
Minimum of 8 years of proven program management experience in the defense, national security, or aerospace domains
Proven track record of successfully managing complex, multi-million-dollar projects and driving their on-time, on-budget completion
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving abilities with the ability to move seamlessly between tactical and the 30,000 ft level
Experience coordinating multiple internal and external teams within a complex engineering or technology-focused organization
Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present complex information clearly and concisely to diverse audiences
Strong technical, analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to use data and metrics to back up assumptions, recommendations and drive decisions
Experience with tools like JIRA and Confluence
Current TS/SCI
Willingness to travel up to 50%

US Salary Range

$183,000—$229,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

new_jobs.title: Assistant Project Manager - Defence and Security
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you.

To find out more about our Property and Buildings business by clicking on the following link and discover what awaits you at WSP: https://www.wsp.com/en-GB/hubs/property-and-buildings

A Little More About Your Role…

We are looking for Assistant Delivery Leads, (Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers), to manage high-value, challenging projects and programmes within the Defence and Security sector. In this role, you will report to the Delivery Lead and be responsible for delivering projects according to the project plan. Assistant Project Managers will either support larger projects and programmes or take the lead on smaller projects as Project Managers depending on experience.

We are looking for proactive individuals who can build strong relationships with clients and internal teams to get tasks scoped and delivered to budget, on time and in line with client expectations and the WSP Business Management System. This is a hands-on role that will see you organising meetings, writing reports, controlling resources and monitoring finances.
You will be responsible for traditional project management activities including but not limited to scope and resource management, finance and schedule monitoring, change control, risk management and client management, overlaid with additional requirements of the Defence and Security sector such as security management.
As part of a growing and diverse team, you will be tackling complex building and infrastructure projects that span the RIBA design stages.

We are relatively new to the sector and are recruiting following several significant wins with both public and private sector clients. As well as delighting our growing client base we are developing a strong defence and security culture within WSP. In this role you will also assist ongoing work winning activities and act as an ambassador for the sector within the business.

We are nationwide and work flexibly between home, WSP and client offices, travelling as required to best deliver the particular needs of the project/programme.

What We Would Be Looking For You To Demonstrate…

Proven experience in the Defence and Security sector assisting in a project management capacity, delivering construction or infrastructure projects (not IT Infrastructure) including a demonstrable understanding of working in accordance with security protocols
Knowledge of any of the following:
MOD policy, processes and procedures
Knowledge of the JSPs, in particular JSP 850
The Green Book and 5 case model for business cases

Degree in relevant technical discipline (engineering, building, quantity surveying, architecture, project or construction management)
Progression towards a recognised project management qualification from one of the following: PMI, APM, RICS, CIOB
Progress towards NEC3/4 PM qualification
An existing network within the Defence and Security sector

You must be eligible to achieve Security Clearance.

Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.

Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact. Our global team includes more than 69,000 employees, working together to make a difference in communities both close to home and around the world.

With us, you can. Apply today.

new_jobs.description:
Department
: Decision & Information Science Salary
: 43,000 - 48,900

Description
:

Manages the day-to-day operations of a small or medium-sized university program or department. May supervise staff employees, student workers, programs or processes.

Plans and develops procedures for administering a small or medium-sized department or program.
Oversees program expenditures and ensures adherence to budget.
Provides guidance to subordinate staff and evaluates performance.
May prepare or participate in the creation of abstracts, research reports, funding proposals, operations and procedure manuals, and other written material and documentation.
Reviews reports of budgets and activities.
Prepares ad hoc reports as needed.
May administer grants and grant-related related communications, scholarships and other operations.
Develops, implements and maintains appropriate policies and procedures.
May serve as property custodian for the department.
Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Description:

Additional Position Information

This position works in the Decision and Information Sciences department at the C. T. Bauer College of Business. The business office is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive individual who will support the business operations management team for the department. This includes financial responsibilities pertaining to voucher processing/service procurement, contract assistance, assisting with event planning, customer service interface, and any other business operations activities to ensure compliance with university policies and procedures.

Successful candidates will have the ability to work independently as well as part of a team, work well under pressure, consistently meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects while remaining flexible and positive. This will require exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail. Further, successful candidates will effectively communicate with all levels of management and fellow employees and be able to manage multiple employer relationships.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who values accuracy, process improvement, and collaboration in supporting academic and research operations.

Position Includes The Following Responsibilities But Not Limited To:

Reconcile Concur expenses for prospective employees and visiting professors.
Initiates financial documents and special vouchers (Vouchers/SC Vouchers/Requisitions/Purchase Orders/P-Card).
Reconcile P-Card expenses (US Bank).
Verifying cost centers with management and obtaining appropriate approvals.

Preferences:

Candidates who are detailed oriented.
Experience with excel and willing to learn.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate policy and procedures.

Qualifications:
Experience will be considered in lieu of education.

Notes to Applicant:
Please include full work history on resume.

Required Attachments:
Cover Letter, Resume

MQ: Education: Requires a thorough understanding of both theoretical and practical aspects of an analytical, technical or professional discipline; or the basic knowledge of more than one professional discipline. Knowledge of the discipline is normally obtained through a formal, directly job-related 4 year degree from a college or university or an equivalent in-depth specialized training program that is directly related to the type of work being performed. Experience: No experience required.

All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check.

The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.
